title: feat(skills): Migrate second common workflow batch
body:
## Summary

Migrate the second validated batch of portable common workflows:

- `git-commit` discovers consumer policy, verifies task-owned changes, stages exact paths, and verifies the resulting commit.
- `create-issue` discovers repository identity, forms, labels, and duplicates before an immutable confirmed create.
- `fix-issue` performs read-only issue preflight, preserves ownership/approval boundaries, and delegates consumer-specific implementation policy.
- `auto-pr` composes the existing commit, PR, and PR-fix workflows with bounded objective repairs and deferred judgment.

Add three shared contracts:

- `lib/repository/policy.md` for consumer policy precedence, ambiguity stops, and change ownership.
- `lib/github/issue-context.md` for host/repository-pinned issue discovery and preflight.
- `lib/github/issue-templates.md` for discovered issue-form fields and required user facts.

Add executable safety helpers for exact-path staging, Git-only issue repository discovery and immutable issue creation, assigned/status/linked-PR preflight, bounded automatic repair ledgers, and compatible host-pinned paginated PR lookup.

## Foreign-repository regression scenarios

- `git-commit`: default branch `trunk`, required `Change-Type:` field, and unrelated user edits remain untouched.
- `create-issue`: a custom issue form, no project board, and a related-but-not-duplicate issue.
- `fix-issue`: a fork checkout, an already-assigned issue, and a repository-specific verification command.
- `auto-pr`: one objective CI failure is repaired while an architecture review request remains unresolved and deferred.

RED pressure tests exposed source-specific commit conventions, incomplete or ambient issue routing, ignored issue ownership/custom-test policy, and duplicated/unbounded PR mechanics. Fresh forward tests for every skill then selected consumer policy, preserved exact host/repository and ownership scope, honored approval/confirmation gates, bounded objective repair, and deferred unresolved judgment.

## Verification

- `python -m unittest discover -s tests -v`: 159 tests passed locally with one expected Bubblewrap-unavailable skip; repeated after the compatibility fix.
- Guarded credential-free Bubblewrap snapshot: 52 focused GitHub/portability tests and all 159 discovered tests passed with no skip.
- `ruff check tests`: passed.
- `ruff format --check tests`: 14 files already formatted.
- `pyright`: 0 errors, 0 warnings, 0 informations.
- Syntax validation passed for every tracked shell script.
- Skill validation passed for `git-commit`, `create-issue`, `fix-issue`, `auto-pr`, and the adjusted `github-pr` workflow.
- `git diff --check origin/main...HEAD` and banned portability scans passed.
- The repaired production PR lookup was verified against GitHub CLI 2.87.3 and the live host-pinned create route.

Consumer repositories are not modified by this pull request.

title: setup.md resolves LOCAL_REPO from the gh default repository, selecting the wrong push target in a fork checkout
body:
## Summary

`lib/github/setup.md` §2 derives `LOCAL_REPO` with `gh repo view --json nameWithOwner,url` (line 39). Invoked with no argument, `gh repo view` returns the **gh default repository**, which `gh repo set-default` stores in the consuming repository's own Git config as `remote.<name>.gh-resolved = base`. In a fork checkout whose default points at the parent, `LOCAL_REPO` becomes the parent — not "the repository represented by this checkout", which is how §2 defines it.

Every downstream derivation inherits the wrong identity. Observed in a fork checkout with `origin = Hzfengsy/pypto` and `upstream = hw-native-sys/pypto`:

| setup.md line | Variable | Expected (fork checkout) | Actual |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 43 | `LOCAL_REPO` | `Hzfengsy/pypto` | `hw-native-sys/pypto` |
| 61 | `IS_FORK` | `true` | `false` |
| 63-67 | `PR_REPO` | `hw-native-sys/pypto` | `hw-native-sys/pypto` |
| 171 | `PUSH_REMOTE` | `origin` | `upstream` |
| 207-213 | `ROLE` / `PR_HEAD_PREFIX` | `fork` / `Hzfengsy:` | `owner` / *(empty)* |

The net effect is that the workflow is configured to push a feature branch **directly into the shared upstream repository** instead of the contributor's fork.

The failure is silent, and the existing guards do not catch it because they verify consistency against the already-wrong identity. `pr-context.sh guard-branch` compares `LOCAL_REPO` with `HEAD_REPO`; both are wrong in the same direction, so it passes. The same applies to the `remote_targets_repo "$PUSH_REMOTE" "$EXPECTED_PUSH_REPO"` check in `commit-and-push.md`, since `EXPECTED_PUSH_REPO` is derived from the same poisoned `LOCAL_REPO`.

## Motivation/Impact

This resolves toward the higher-blast-radius target: it silently redirects a push from a personal fork to a shared organization repository. A contributor who follows the documented workflow can create branches directly on the upstream repo without any step reporting the change of destination.

`gh repo set-default` is not an exotic configuration. `gh` interactively prompts for it the first time you run `gh pr list` / `gh issue list` in a checkout with more than one remote, so any fork clone with both `origin` and `upstream` is a candidate. The setting lives in the consuming repository's Git config, so it is invisible to anyone reading only the skill sources.

Reproduction, entirely read-only:

```bash
cd <fork-checkout>            # origin=<you>/<repo>, upstream=<org>/<repo>
git config --local --get-regexp 'remote.*gh-resolved'
# remote.upstream.gh-resolved base

gh repo view --json nameWithOwner --jq .nameWithOwner
# <org>/<repo>                <-- the parent, not this checkout

gh repo view --json nameWithOwner --jq .nameWithOwner --repo <you>/<repo>
# <you>/<repo>                <-- what setup.md §2 intends
```

Found while running `auto-pr` against `hw-native-sys/pypto`. It was caught only because the operator inspected `git remote -v` by hand before the push and noticed the mismatch; nothing in the workflow surfaced it.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `LOCAL_REPO` is derived from the checkout's own remotes (for example the remote the current branch tracks, else `origin`), not from an argument-less `gh repo view`.
- When the checkout-derived identity and the gh default repository disagree, the workflow stops with an actionable message naming both values, rather than silently preferring either one.
- A fork checkout with `remote.<upstream>.gh-resolved = base` resolves `ROLE=fork`, `PUSH_REMOTE=origin`, `PR_HEAD_PREFIX=<owner>:`, and `PR_REPO=<parent>`.
- A non-fork checkout with the same setting still resolves `ROLE=owner` correctly.
- `lib/github/setup.md` §2 documents the interaction with `gh repo set-default` and states that the gh default repository is not a source of checkout identity.
- Regression coverage under `tests/` (alongside `test_github_pr.py` / `test_commit_and_push.py`) for the fork-with-`gh-resolved`-parent topology.

title: Validation sandbox cannot run validation for native-build repositories, and its documented escape hatch has no mechanism
body:
## Summary

`lib/github/commit-and-push.md` requires the push transaction to validate inside `scripts/validation-sandbox.sh`, forbids any credentialed fallback, and offers exactly one escape hatch: "stop and require an explicitly trusted project runner that enforces the same credential-free, network-denied boundary". No mechanism exists to declare such a runner, so for any repository whose validation needs a native build the workflow has no supported path to completion.

Measured against `hw-native-sys/pypto` (C++ extension built with CMake + nanobind, one Git submodule). Every element of that repository's documented validation fails inside the sandbox:

| Repository-defined validation | Sandbox result | Cause |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `cmake -B build -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=RelWithDebInfo` | `Configuring incomplete, errors occurred!` | `find_package(nanobind CONFIG REQUIRED)` fails; nanobind lives in the host Python environment, which the sandbox correctly hides |
| C++ link step | would fail | `3rdparty/msgpack-c` is empty — `git archive` does not include submodule contents |
| `python -m pytest tests/ut/` | cannot run | `pytest` absent; no network to install it |
| `python tests/lint/check_headers.py` | `Error: '/workspace' is not a git repository` | the repo's own lint scripts enumerate via `git ls-files`; the sandbox strips Git metadata by design |

The last row is the notable one: even the pure-Python checks fail, so this is not merely "native builds are hard". Probed by invoking `validation-sandbox.sh` directly with a diagnostic command; `bwrap` 0.8.0 was present and working, so this is not a missing-runtime case.

Two distinguishable problems:

1. **No way to declare a trusted runner.** The contract names the escape hatch but provides no config key, file, or convention for supplying one, and correctly forbids selecting one from the worktree. The instruction is therefore unactionable.
2. **`git archive` silently drops submodule contents.** `validation-sandbox.sh` builds the snapshot with `git archive --format=tar "$PREPARED_HEAD_OID"`. For a repository with submodules the extracted tree is incomplete, and the omission is silent — validation could fail for a reason unrelated to the change, or in principle pass while never compiling the omitted code.

A third, ordering issue: sandbox feasibility is knowable before any repository mutation, but the blocker surfaces at the push gate. In the observed run a branch had already been created, changes staged, and a commit written before the workflow discovered it could not validate or push.

## Motivation/Impact

`pypto-developer` is published for `hw-native-sys/pypto`, and `auto-pr` / `github-pr` / `fix-pr` cannot complete their push transaction there. The operator's only options are to abandon the workflow or to override the documented boundary, and the second is what actually happened in the observed run — which is the outcome the boundary exists to prevent. An unactionable safety rule tends to get bypassed rather than obeyed.

The submodule gap is independently worth fixing: it silently changes what gets validated, for any consumer with submodules, whether or not the trusted-runner question is resolved.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A documented mechanism exists for a repository to declare a trusted validation runner, resolved from a location outside the consuming worktree so the existing threat model is preserved, and `commit-and-push.md` references it where it currently says "require an explicitly trusted project runner".
- `validation-sandbox.sh` produces a complete snapshot for a repository with submodules, or fails loudly when it cannot, rather than silently extracting an incomplete tree.
- The skills detect that validation cannot run in the available sandbox **before** creating a branch, staging, or committing, and report it while the worktree is still unmodified.
- The reported blocker names which specific validation requirement could not be met (missing toolchain, submodule contents, Git metadata, or network) instead of a generic failure.
- `tests/test_commit_and_push.py` covers the submodule snapshot case and the declared-runner path.

title: feat(skills): Sharpen PR description, publication, and recheck contracts
body:
## Summary

Four `pypto-developer` contracts let published work go out unclear or
unreviewed. Pull-request bodies were generated as a bullet list of commit
subjects, so a single-commit PR published a body identical to its title.
`auto-pr` stopped to ask for approval of the branch name and commit set even
though it is the unattended entry point. `create-issue` gated creation behind an
approval token echoed back to its helper. `fix-pr` let a checks-only poll stand
in for its final recheck, so a review landing minutes after publication had no
path to surface. After this change reviewers get a description that explains the
change, unattended publication stays unattended, an issue previews as plain
text, and no wait can hide feedback.

## Changes

- `lib/github/pr-description.md` (new) owns title and body composition from the
  commit range and its diff. It requires Summary, Changes, and Verification
  sections, preserves human-authored bodies on the update route, and stops
  publication when the body is empty or equal to the title. `github-pr` now
  delegates to it instead of emitting `git log --format='- %s'`, and
  `git-commit` asks for a message body when the subject cannot carry why the
  change is needed, since descriptions derive from those messages.
- `auto-pr` supplies `github-pr` standing authorization covering branch naming,
  the commit set and its message, and the description; it requires a
  reviewer-ready description and reports the branch and commit subjects it
  published. `lib/github/branch-naming.md` and `git-commit` accept that
  authorization and continue without prompting, while ownership separation,
  policy, and verification stop rules stay in force.
- `create-issue` posts the complete issue directly as text; `issue-create.sh`
  takes no approval token and its preview route and payload hash are gone.
  Target validation, control-character rejection, the private body snapshot,
  and the outcome markers are unchanged, so drift between the shown text and
  the created issue is now a contract rule rather than a hash check.
- `fix-pr` re-runs the complete feedback inventory on every poll while checks
  are pending, treats a checks-only poll as never a recheck, and no longer
  treats green checks alone as terminal. `lib/github/fetch-comments.md`
  documents that an inventory taken minutes after creation or a push is
  provisional. `auto-pr`'s loop step and green-success condition match.
- Rebased onto #7: the validation-runner paragraphs in `fix-pr` and `github-pr`
  keep that pull request's working-checkout wording, not the removed sandbox
  wording.
- Follow-up commit `497a394`, answering review feedback on the first: `create`
  records the complete payload it is about to publish, read back from the
  private snapshot, before the mutation boundary, and fails closed when it
  cannot. Removing the token means publication is no longer bound to the
  approved text; this makes a divergence visible rather than silent. It does
  not restore the binding, which stays a deliberate decision.
- `dbf9cea` and `90bbbe4` fix two defects review found in that record, both of
  which let it claim an exactness the publication path did not deliver. The
  body no longer passes through command substitution, which stripped every
  trailing newline: it is copied out verbatim under a declared
  `Body (N bytes):` length. A label whose name contains a comma is now rejected
  during validation, because `gh issue create --help` documents
  `--label "bug,help wanted"` as the form for two labels, so the CLI would
  apply a label set the record never named.

## Verification

- `python -m unittest discover -s tests`: 205 tests, OK
- `ruff check tests`: All checks passed
- `ruff format --check tests`: 13 files already formatted
- `pyright`: 0 errors, 0 warnings, 0 informations
- `git ls-files -z -- '*.sh' | xargs -0 -r -n 1 bash -n`: exit 0

All five ran again inside the push transaction's worktree validation at the
pushed commit.

title: feat(skills): Gate repository mutations on PTO scope and release 0.2.0
body:
## Summary

Developer skills previously acted on whatever repository happened to be checked
out: an invocation aimed at one project could commit, push, delete branches, file
issues, or write pull-request state in an unrelated one without ever saying so.
This adds a shared repository scope gate that every writing skill resolves before
its first mutation, so those workflows run on their own authority only in a
PTO-family repository and stop for explicit confirmation anywhere else. It also
gives the repository a written release procedure and publishes both plugins as
`0.2.0`, so consumers still installed on the `0.1.0` contracts can pick this up.

Callers in a PTO-family repository see no behavior change. Callers elsewhere now
get a warning naming the repository, its remotes, the classifying evidence, and
the exact intended mutation, and nothing is written until they confirm.

## Changes

- `lib/repository/scope.md`: new scope authority. Classifies a checkout from its
  directory name, every configured fetch and push URL, and its own governing
  instruction files. Fails closed — an unresolved identity or a failed command
  classifies as foreign rather than passing unclassified.
- Confirmation semantics: scoped to one repository and one invocation, so it
  cannot carry to another repository, skill, invocation, or session. An
  autonomous caller's standing authorization explicitly does not cover the gate;
  such a run in a foreign repository reports it as a blocker instead of
  confirming on the user's behalf. Read-only inspection stays ungated.
- `lib/repository/policy.md`, `lib/github/setup.md`: both shared contracts route
  through the gate, so a skill that loads only one still resolves it.
- `skills/{auto-pr,clean-branches,create-issue,fix-issue,fix-pr,git-commit,github-pr}`:
  each writing skill references the gate at its own first-write point.
  `create-issue` moves no Git object, but filing an issue writes to a remote
  repository and notifies its watchers, which is the same exposure.
- `tests/test_portability.py`: three new tests pin the gate — every writing skill
  links it, both shared contracts route through it, and the gate keeps its
  fail-closed and confirmation-scope guarantees. The portable instruction budget
  moves from 200 to 210 lines because `fix-pr` and `github-pr` sat at exactly 200
  and could not otherwise carry the gate.
- `.claude/skills/release/SKILL.md`: repository-local release skill, deliberately
  outside both published plugins so it never ships. It locates the four
  manifests, derives the change set since the current version was set, presents
  patch/minor/major candidates with one recommended, and leaves the choice to the
  user rather than bumping on its own.
- `.gitignore`: ignore `.claude/worktrees/`; the existing `.worktrees/` pattern
  does not match that path, so the release skill could not be committed without
  sweeping in the linked worktree checkout beside it.
- Plugin manifests: `pypto-developer` and `pypto-user` both move to `0.2.0`
  across their Claude and Codex manifests, on one shared version line. Minor
  rather than patch: the gate can halt a workflow that previously ran unattended,
  and that belongs in the version string rather than being discovered at the
  first foreign checkout.

## Verification

Run by the push transaction's validation runner in the checkout at the pushed
commit `720ddba`:

- `python -m unittest discover -s tests`: exit 0 — 208 tests OK
- `ruff check tests`: exit 0 — all checks passed
- `ruff format --check tests`: exit 0 — 13 files already formatted
- `pyright`: exit 0 — 0 errors, 0 warnings
- `git ls-files -z -- '*.sh' | xargs -0 -r -n 1 bash -n`: exit 0

The scope classifier was additionally exercised against four scratch checkouts:
this repository and a checkout whose only marker is a remote URL both classify
as family; a repository declaring the family only in its README classifies as
family; an unrelated `cryptography` checkout classifies as foreign.

title: fix(skills): Resolve the push target from Git remotes
body:
## Summary

Repository identity for the pull-request workflows came from `gh repo view`,
which resolves the GitHub CLI's *base* repository rather than the repository a
checkout pushes to. In a fork checkout that also has an upstream remote `gh`
prefers the parent, so `LOCAL_REPO` became the upstream, `PUSH_REMOTE` pointed
at it, `ROLE` stayed `owner`, and the fork disappeared from publication,
lookup, and repair alike; when several remotes qualify and no default is set,
`gh` stops to ask which base repository to use, which turns an unattended run
into a prompt. Identity now comes from the Git remotes through one resolver
shared by the pull-request and issue workflows: a fork checkout pushes to its
fork and targets the parent, and a checkout with nothing writable stops during
setup with the remedy named instead of continuing until Git refuses the push.

## Changes

- `lib/github/scripts/repo-identity.sh`: new resolver. `resolve
  [--require-push]` reads every remote fetch and push URL, pins one host,
  validates each candidate through host-pinned REST metadata, and reports
  `github_host`, `local_repo`, `base_repo`, `is_fork`, `local_can_push`, and
  `default_branch`. With `--require-push` the write target is chosen by
  evidence: a fork the authenticated account both owns and can push to wins.
  Write access is not ownership — an account can be a collaborator on somebody
  else's fork — so a fork owned by another account is rejected whether it is
  the only writable one or one of several. More than one owned writable fork is
  an error rather than a guess, the base repository wins only when the account
  can push to it, and with nothing writable the resolver fails, naming the base
  repository and every fork remote it rejected.
- `lib/github/setup.md`: section 2 consumes that resolver with `--require-push`
  instead of `gh repo view`, and no longer derives the host, fork state, or
  default branch itself. `LOCAL_REPO` is now the verified writable repository,
  so section 3 selects the fork remote as `PUSH_REMOTE` when a fork exists.
- `lib/github/scripts/issue-context.sh`: `repository` delegates to the same
  resolver and reshapes its output to the unchanged `github_host`,
  `local_repo`, `issue_repo`, `default_branch` contract, so issue and
  pull-request identity cannot drift. Without push evidence the read-only rule
  is unchanged: a fork remote still identifies the checkout.
- `lib/github/issue-context.md`, `lib/github/common-issues.md`: document the
  delegation and add diagnostics for a checkout with no writable repository and
  for several writable fork remotes.
- `tests/test_repo_identity.py`: 15 executable cases over a fake `gh` and real
  Git remotes — fork beside upstream, upstream-only, unwritable upstream, an
  unwritable foreign fork remote, a sole *writable* fork owned by another
  account both with and without a writable base, nothing writable, two owned
  writable forks, one owned among several, none owned among several, read-only
  resolution, unrelated hosts, unrelated repositories, no remotes, and usage
  errors.
- `tests/test_portability.py`: `setup.md` may now consume `REPO_IDENTITY_HELPER`;
  new assertions pin the resolver's presence and executability, the
  `--require-push` call, the documented selection rule, the issue-side
  delegation, and a repository-wide invariant that no deployable shell calls
  `gh repo view`.

No interface changes for callers of the skills: `setup.md` produces the same
context variables, and `issue-context.sh repository` returns the same JSON
shape. Consumers pick this up when the plugin version they have installed is
updated; this change does not bump the plugin version.

Review feedback addressed in `f037c85`: ownership is verified in the single-writable-fork case too, so write access to somebody else's fork never selects it as the push target.

## Verification

- `python -m ruff check tests`: 0, All checks passed
- `python -m ruff format --check tests`: 0, 15 files already formatted
- `python -m pyright`: 0, 0 errors, 0 warnings, 0 informations
- `git ls-files -z -- '*.sh' | xargs -0 -r -n 1 bash -n`: 0
- `python -m unittest discover -s tests`: 0, 230 tests OK
- The same set ran again inside each push transaction's validation runner at
  the pushed commit, and passed both times.
- `repo-identity.sh resolve --require-push` in three live checkouts: a fork
  checkout with an upstream remote resolved to the fork with the parent as
  base, a second fork checkout did the same, and a checkout with only an
  upstream remote resolved to that repository with `is_fork` false.
